objects.docstring:
poetry's reactive tier: server actions for any component that implements
`render_in` (ViewComponent, and anything else that speaks the Rails
renderable protocol), on poetry's exact stack - one generic Stimulus
controller, one endpoint, Turbo-Stream replace-by-id.

The security spine (the reason this layer exists - it is also the
contract poetry's operate / Gen-UI runtime rides):

  * The DOM carries a signed IDENTITY, never a state snapshot: a record's
    GlobalID (re-found server-side on every action - state lives in the
    DB) and/or the declared state ivars, in ONE MessageVerifier payload.
  * Actions are DEFAULT-DENY: only methods declared `action :name` are
    invokable; everything else is 403 before any code runs.
  * Params pass a declared schema and are coerced server-side; undeclared
    keys never reach the method (no mass assignment).

The interaction model and wire protocol are adapted from an
MIT-licensed reference design (source and license in
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), reworked for the render_in contract and
poetry's conventions.

methods.name: action_path=
methods.docstring:
The path the actions endpoint mounts at. Components carry it as a
Stimulus value, so changing it needs no client wiring.

methods.name: action_route_ok?
methods.docstring:
True when a POST to `path` resolves to the gem's ActionsController.
A host catch-all route appended above the engine's route SHADOWS it,
so every reactive POST 404s with nothing in the log - this is the
signal that turns that opaque failure into a one-line warning.

methods.name: authorization_errors
methods.docstring:
Exception classes the endpoint renders as 403. Append your
authorization library's error (Pundit::NotAuthorizedError, ...).
The token proves the identity is OURS - authorization that this user
may act belongs in the action itself; raise and it becomes a 403.

methods.name: authorization_errors=
methods.docstring:
Exception classes the endpoint renders as 403. Append your
authorization library's error (Pundit::NotAuthorizedError, ...).
The token proves the identity is OURS - authorization that this user
may act belongs in the action itself; raise and it becomes a 403.

methods.name: base_controller
methods.docstring:
The resolved base controller class (see base_controller_name; the
actions endpoint's superclass).

methods.name: base_controller_name=
methods.docstring:
The controller the actions endpoint inherits from, as a String
(resolved lazily to dodge load-order). Default ActionController::Base;
set to "ApplicationController" to inherit the host's auth/CSRF - but
make sure the action path isn't force-redirected for signed-out users
if any reactive component renders on public pages.

methods.name: loader
methods.docstring: The dedicated Zeitwerk loader for poetry-reactive's lib/ tree.

methods.name: root
methods.docstring: Gem root (the directory containing lib/, app/, config/).

methods.name: sign
methods.docstring: Sign an identity payload hash into a token.

methods.name: verifier=
methods.docstring:
The message verifier that signs/verifies component identity tokens.
Defaults to a purpose-scoped verifier derived from secret_key_base.

methods.name: verify
methods.docstring: The verified payload hash, or nil when the token is invalid.

methods.name: warn_unless_action_route_mounted!
methods.docstring:
Log a clear warning (once, at boot) when the action path doesn't
resolve to the gem controller. Called from the engine's
after_initialize; no-op when the route is fine.

constants.name: ACTIONS_CONTROLLER
constants.docstring:
The controller a correctly-mounted action path resolves to (the boot
guard below checks this).

constants.name: IDENTITY_PURPOSE
constants.docstring:
Purpose string bound into every identity token's signature, so a token
minted here can never be replayed against another verifier use.

objects.docstring:
The single endpoint behind every reactive component. The generic
`poetry--reactive` Stimulus controller POSTs here with a signed
identity token, an action name, and params. We verify the token,
rebuild the component (re-finding the record via GlobalID for
record-backed components), run the whitelisted action, and return an
auto-targeted Turbo-Stream replace the client applies.

Failure surface (the security contract, mechanically):
  * tampered/foreign token            -> 400 (nothing else runs)
  * undeclared action                 -> 403 (default-deny)
  * record no longer locatable        -> 404
  * action raised an authz error      -> 403 (Poetry::Reactive.authorization_errors)

The token proves the identity is OURS - not that this user may act.
Authorization belongs IN the action (raise; it renders as 403 here).
Inherit from the host's ApplicationController (set
Poetry::Reactive.base_controller_name) to get its auth/CSRF/Current.

methods.name: create
methods.docstring:
The one endpoint action: verify the token, resolve the component
class, gate on the declared action (default-deny), rebuild the
component, coerce the params, run the action in a transaction, and
answer with the Turbo-Stream replace. The rescue clauses implement
the failure table in the class docs.

objects.docstring:
Schema coercion for action params - the third leg of the security spine
(signed identity, default-deny, schema-coerce). Client params are
coerced against the action's declared schema; anything undeclared is
dropped, so no raw mass assignment ever reaches a component action.

A type is one of:
  * a scalar symbol      :string / :integer / :float / :boolean
  * a Hash schema        { id: :integer, ... }  - nested object
  * a one-element Array  [:integer] / [{ ... }] - array of that type

Arrays accept both a real JSON array and a Rails-style index hash
({ "0" => ..., "1" => ... }); flat bracketed keys from a model-scoped
form ("note[title]") are expanded before matching. The governing rule:
a declared key whose value can't be coerced to its type is DROPPED -
the method's keyword default applies, exactly as if the client had
omitted it - never fabricated into a surprise value.

methods.name: array_values
methods.docstring:
Normalize an array param: a real array passes through; a Rails index
hash ({ "0" => ..., "1" => ... }) becomes its values in index order.
Anything else (a stray scalar, nil) is malformed -> nil, so the
caller drops the param.

methods.name: bracket_path
methods.docstring:
Split a flat form key into its path: "items[0][qty]" ->
["items", "0", "qty"]; a bracket-less key is its own path.

methods.name: call
methods.docstring:
Coerce the request's params against an action's schema. Returns the
symbol-keyed kwargs the action is invoked with.

methods.name: coerce
methods.docstring: Dispatch one declared type: array, nested hash, or scalar.

methods.name: coerce_array
methods.docstring:
A real array (or Rails index hash) coerces element-wise. A malformed
present-but-non-array value returns DROP rather than [] - coercing a
stray scalar to an empty array would let a bad payload read as an
explicit "clear everything". An element that coerces to DROP is
rejected; an array whose EVERY element drops returns DROP (the
keyword default applies), while a genuinely empty input stays [].

methods.name: coerce_hash
methods.docstring:
Keep declared keys only, recursing for nested hash/array types.
Symbolizes keys to splat as kwargs. A key whose value coerces to DROP
is skipped (the keyword default applies).

methods.name: coerce_scalar
methods.docstring:
Cast one scalar value to its declared type (booleans via
ActiveModel's cast, so "0"/"false"/"" behave like Rails forms).

methods.name: deep_assign
methods.docstring:
Assign a value at a nested path, building intermediate hashes and
merging collisions via merge_value.

methods.name: expand_bracket_keys
methods.docstring:
"note[title]" => { "note" => { "title" => ... } };
"items[0][qty]" nests into the index-hash form array_values already
understands. Deep-merges so sibling bracket keys coalesce; keys
without brackets and already-nested values pass through untouched.

methods.name: merge_value
methods.docstring:
Two hashes deep-merge (bracket-expanded fields and a pre-nested
object for the same key both survive); any other collision takes the
new value.

methods.name: to_param_hash
methods.docstring:
Unwrap ActionController::Parameters (or a plain Hash) to a
string-keyed Hash, then expand bracket notation so a model-scoped
Rails form's flat keys ("note[title]") nest before exact-key matching.

methods.name: validate_schema!
methods.docstring:
Validate a declared schema at action-declaration time, so an
unsupported type is a load-time error with the component named,
not a request-time surprise.

constants.name: BRACKET_SEGMENT
constants.docstring: One segment of a bracketed key ("items[0][qty]" has three).

constants.name: DROP
constants.docstring: Sentinel for "this value could not be coerced - drop the key".

objects.docstring:
Component turns a server-rendered component (anything implementing `render_in` - a ViewComponent, a poetry-ui component, ...) into a reactive unit: declare actions in Ruby, spread the root/trigger/field attribute helpers into the markup, and the generic `poetry--reactive` Stimulus controller wires DOM events to an HTTP round trip that re-renders the component and replaces it in the DOM by its id. === The security model (the decisive design choice) === Component STATE never ships to the browser. The DOM carries a signed IDENTITY: * Record-backed (the common case): `reactive_record :note` signs the record's GlobalID. The server re-finds it on every action - the client can neither forge the component class nor swap the record. State = the database. * State-backed (record-less, e.g. a counter): `reactive_state :count` signs the listed instance variables. * Both (the inline-edit pattern): a record's GlobalID AND the transient mode ("which field / editing?") in one token, so the mode is tamper-proof alongside the record. Actions are DEFAULT-DENY: only methods declared with `action :name` are client-invokable. The signature proves the token is OURS, not that this user may act - authorize inside the action (raise; the endpoint renders it as 403 via Poetry::Reactive.authorization_errors). Action params pass a declared schema (Poetry::Reactive::Coercion); nothing else reaches the method. Usage (record-backed inline edit): class NoteRowComponent < ViewComponent::Base include Poetry::Reactive::Component reactive_record :note reactive_state :editing action :edit action :save, params: { title: :string } def initialize(note:, editing: false) @note = note @editing = editing end def id = dom_id(@note) def edit = (@editing = true) def save(title:) = (@note.update!(title:); @editing = false) end Template (string-keyed hashes - pass them positionally, don't splat):

methods.name: action
methods.docstring:
Declare a client-invokable action with an optional param schema.

Types: :string / :integer / :float / :boolean scalars, a Hash for a
nested object, a one-element Array for an array of its element type.
The schema is validated at DECLARATION, so an unsupported type is a
load-time error, not a request-time surprise.

params.name: name
params.text:
the public method to expose (actions
are default-deny; undeclared methods stay uninvokable)

params.name: params
params.text:
the param schema the
endpoint coerces client params against

methods.name: from_identity
methods.docstring:
Rebuild a component instance from a verified identity payload
(called by the actions endpoint after signature verification).
Assembles init kwargs from whichever identity pieces are declared:
the re-found record, the signed state, or both.

methods.name: reactive_action
methods.docstring: Look up one declared action.

methods.name: reactive_action?
methods.docstring: Whether an action of this name was declared.

methods.name: reactive_actions
methods.docstring: All declared actions by name, superclass declarations included.

methods.name: reactive_record
methods.docstring:
Declare the (GlobalID-locatable) record this component is rebuilt
from. The signed token carries its GlobalID; the server re-finds it
on each action. State lives in the DB.

params.name: name
params.text:
the initialize keyword the record
arrives as (and the `@ivar` it is read back from)

methods.name: reactive_record_key
methods.docstring:
The declared record keyword (inherited from the superclass when
undeclared here), or nil for record-less components.

methods.name: reactive_state
methods.docstring:
Opt instance variables into the signed identity (record-less
components, or transient mode alongside a record).

methods.name: reactive_state_keys
methods.docstring: The declared state ivar names, superclass declarations included.

methods.name: reactive_field
methods.docstring:
Bind a form control's `name` to an action param so its value travels
with any trigger inside this root (the client auto-collects named
fields, scoped to this component - never a nested reactive root's).

params.name: param
params.text: the action param this control feeds

methods.name: reactive_root_attributes
methods.docstring:
Root-element attributes: the component's id (the replace target), the
generic controller, the signed identity token, and the action path.
String-keyed so it splats into tag.attributes / content_tag and merges
into poetry-core's html_attributes alike.

The id is REQUIRED on the same element (the client self-matches its
next token by the root's id; the server targets it) - a missing id is
raised here, at render, instead of surfacing as a silent 403 on the
second click.

methods.name: reactive_trigger
methods.signature: reactive_trigger(action_name, event: "click", debounce: nil, confirm: nil, **params)
methods.docstring:
Attributes for an element that triggers a declared action.
  <button <%= tag.attributes(**reactive_trigger(:toggle)) %>>...</button>
  reactive_trigger(:save, event: "submit")
  reactive_trigger(:filter, event: "input", debounce: 300)
  reactive_trigger(:destroy, confirm: "Really?")

Extra keyword args become explicit params merged over collected form
fields. Click triggers force type="button" so a bare button inside a
<form> can't native-submit and navigate.

params.name: action_name
params.text:
a declared action (undeclared
names raise at render - actions are default-deny)

params.name: event
params.text: the DOM event that fires the action

params.name: params
params.text: explicit params merged over collected fields

objects.docstring:
The Rails engine: mounts the actions route, exposes the client
runtime to the asset pipeline and importmap, and runs the
route-shadowing boot guard.

The gem's base error class; a misconfigured component (missing #id,
undeclared action in reactive_trigger) raises it at render time.

Raised when a signed identity token fails verification (tampered,
foreign, or signed for another purpose) - the endpoint renders 400.
